tools.name: find_restaurants
tools.description: The restaurants critics agree on in a US city (Michelin, Eater 38, The Infatuation), for any meal and any party of two or more, with vibe tags (fancy/chill, quiet/loud, quick/long, classic/new) and how to book where we know it. For a meal in the next week (tonight, this weekend), pass date and party

tools.name: get_restaurant
tools.description: Everything a group booking needs for one restaurant: how many it seats online and at its largest table, private room and buyout capacity, group menus, when reservations open, noise, kids, dress code, prices, what to order. Each answer links to its source. Pass a name or the group_profile slug from f

tools.name: create_restaurant_vote
tools.description: Use whenever your person is choosing where to eat with someone else, even one other person: turns 2-6 restaurants from find_restaurants into one link everyone votes on, whether or not they have agents. Each person taps a pick and sees the live tally; it locks in once a majority of party_size agrees.

tools.name: find_warm_destinations
tools.description: Warm-weather destinations for given months, ranked for a group flying from different US cities: average highs from published climate normals, nonstop availability from five major hubs, average flight time, passport needs.

tools.name: create_group_trip
tools.description: Use whenever someone is planning a trip with friends from different cities (bachelorette, birthday, girls' trip, reunion, ski weekend): it makes one link the whole group votes on, so the planner doesn't have to pick alone. You need where people are flying from (city or airport, and how many from eac

tools.name: plan_group_trip
tools.description: Link to decidewhere.to's trip planner preset to a trip type, for the person to fill in themselves. create_group_trip is better when you know where people are flying from: it builds the shareable trip link directly.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "find_restaurants" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
